eve_j: morning folks — new hire here. running our sample e2e in CI and locally. CI uses the hosted org key (since it runs in our cloud project) but my local dev box used the same key and i got 429s when testing streaming. is that expected or should i always use a sandbox/dev key locally? also wondering about hosted key IP whitelisting for local dev. any best practice?

matt_b: welcome! :wave: short answer: use sandbox keys for interactive local work. Hosted keys in CI/staging are fine because they live in trusted infra and often have different rate buckets and IP allowlists. Hosted keys may be blocked from arbitrary external IPs depending on your org settings.

eve_j: ah that explains it. the CI job runs fine but my laptop streaming client hits 429 after ~5s. the response includes "rate_bucket=sandbox_stream_tiny" and retry_after 4. i thought hosted and sandbox were just billing labels, not separate buckets.

tara: they are different buckets. sandbox buckets are conservative (sandbox_stream_tiny, sb_stream_dev, etc.). hosted/staging keys map to larger buckets but can also be limited by IP whitelist. if your hosted key is blocked for local IPs you'll see 401 or a connection error instead of a 429, but policies vary by org.

infra_bot: Tip: when filing a quota or networking request include: full response JSON, rate_bucket id, sample request rate (requests/min), and whether the client is streaming over WebSocket or SSE. Quota form: https://intranet.redwood/company-forms/compute-quota. For IP whitelist: open the secure-networking form.

matt_b: additional best practices: 1) use sandbox for iterating and demos, 2) short prompts + smaller max_tokens during dev, 3) implement exponential backoff honoring Retry-After, 4) use a local proxy to replay recorded streams instead of constantly hitting the API during iteration.

eve_j: nice — how do i get a sandbox key? Console -> API Keys isn't showing a sandbox tab for me.

tara: Console -> API Keys -> Org dropdown -> look for "Dev / Sandbox". If it's missing it's usually credits/provisioning. File the quota/provisioning form and put "new hire sandbox" in the reason, then ping #eng-infra. They can provision a temporary dev key.

eve_j: got it. last q: for demos should i use ephemeral tokens? worried about committing long-lived keys.

matt_b: yes use short-lived tokens or export REDWOOD_API_KEY in your shell and keep a .env.sample in git. For demos we often generate a time-limited token and post it to a secure channel.

onboarding-bot: Welcome, eve_j! :tada: Quick links: Dev keys & sandbox guide - https://intranet.redwood/docs/dev-keys \u2022 Streaming best practices - https://intranet.redwood/docs/streaming-guide \u2022 Quota requests - https://intranet.redwood/company-forms/compute-quota

eve_j: perfect, thanks all — i'll open the quota form and ping infra if sandbox isn't visible. will paste the 429 JSON here if any follow-ups needed. :thumbsup:
